subject: AuroraFin request: forensic pack for tenant key revocation scenarios
messages:
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey.park@aurorafin.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sec-ops@aurorafin.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Forensic pack request: tenant KEK revocation + operator trail

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of AuroraFin's SIG submission we need a concise forensic package that demonstrates Redwood's handling of a tenant key encryption key (KEK) revocation scenario and operator-access telemetry around that event. The checklist we shared covers the broad asks; to make things actionable for our audit team, could you deliver the following artifacts scoped to a representative tenant (redacted IDs is fine):

- chronological timeline of the revocation event (timestamps in ISO) and the exact runbook steps that the platform executed (who/what initiated rotation, principal, and any automated fallbacks)
- KMS audit logs filtered to the tenant's KEK for the 48 hours around the event (include request IDs and GRPC/REST call traces where available)
- HSM attestation / tamper log excerpt for the shift window when the rotation occurred
- KV-cache eviction traces (kvcache prefixes and cache-hit metrics) showing prefix invalidation after the new KEK is applied
- sample wrapped key object metadata (no plaintext) showing wrapping algorithm and cipher-suite used in transit
- operator access trail (IDs of operator principals, IPs, and justifications) and any recorded session transcripts or jump-host references

If possible we prefer delivery via SFTP (details above) or a signed Drive link. Our auditors would like a short narrative (1–2 pages) that maps each artifact to the SIG question it satisfies. Do you have an estimate for delivery and any blockers we should be aware of?

Appreciate it — Lindsey
Lindsey Park
Security Director, AuroraFin

--
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lindsey Park <lindsey.park@aurorafin.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic pack request: tenant KEK revocation + operator trail

Lindsey —

Thanks for the clear list. We can produce a focused pack that addresses each bullet. Quick notes and deliverable plan:

1) What we'll provide (package):
   - rotation_runbook_v2.pdf (annotated runbook with timestamps and automation hooks)
   - kms_access_audit_202807.zip (filtered KMS audit events + mapping table)
   - hsm_tamper_log_excerpt.csv (redacted event rows around rotation window)
   - kvcache_eviction_traces.log (excerpt showing prefix invalidation)
   - wrapped_key_samples.jsonl (metadata-only samples, no plaintext)
   - operator_access_index.md (access principal list + IPs + session ids)
   - forensic_inquiry_checklist.md (narrative mapping artifacts to SIG/CAIQ items)

2) Timeline: we can assemble the first pass by end of day Thu, Jul 27. Final sanitized archive by Mon, Jul 31 after internal review. If you need earlier, we can provide the runbook + timestamps first (ETA Wed, Jul 26).

3) Delivery method: SFTP is fine — we'll stage under your path and send a TTL-signed Drive link for the narrative.

4) Potential blockers: cross-team review required for HSM exports (security operations) and legal review on what metadata we can disclose for operator sessions. We'll mark those sections redacted if necessary but will include audit identifiers to map back to originals.

Jonas and Kimberly — looping you in for HSM log export and KMS audit slicing. Jon, can you confirm the operator session retention window we can share? Kim, please confirm the wrapping metadata format we'll include.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Trust & Safety Program Manager
Redwood Inference

--
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic pack request: tenant KEK revocation + operator trail

Marissa / team —

I pulled the HSM window for the candidate tenant (ID redacted) and can confirm: we retain tamper/timestamp logs for 90 days by default; the cryptographic module writes shift-level entries and operator session handles to /var/log/hsm-shifts/ and we can export a CSV excerpt with the following columns: event_time (ISO), event_type, operator_principal, session_id, hsm_slot, tamper_flag, signature_blob_id. We'll include the signature_blob_id references (not raw blobs) so auditors can correlate with the attestation chain without receiving sensitive key material.

For operator sessions: we keep session start/stop, invoked commands, and jump-host source IPs for 30 days. Legal has approved metadata disclosure for audits when coupled with a non-disclosure addendum (we've historically used the standard AuroraFin NDA addendum). If you need longer retention snapshots, we can request an exceptional export but that adds 2 business days.

On wrapping metadata: we use AES-GCM 256 for KEK wrapping in transit with RSA-ECIES for key-encryption under HSM-managed signing. Kimberly, I'll pull the example jsonl schema and attach it to the package.

Jonas
Principal Cryptography Engineer

--
From: Lindsey Park <lindsey.park@aurorafin.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: sec-ops@aurorafin.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic pack request: tenant KEK revocation + operator trail

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick alignment and the delivery dates. Wed, Jul 26 for the runbook + timestamps works for our auditors; full package by Mon, Jul 31 is fine. We'll get the NDA addendum signed and route it back to you today so you can include the operator session metadata without redaction.

One small ask: could you include a short example of the KMS REST request/response pair (IDs only, no tokens) for the revocation call so our integrators can match request IDs to traffic traces on our side? That will make reconciliation much faster.

Thanks again — looking forward to the package.

Lindsey
Security Director, AuroraFin
